_readme: What's new, written for the person using Retake — not for whoever wrote it. Both the landing page and the Retake window read THIS file; there is no second copy. Rules for adding one: say what changed for them, name no files, no flags they will not type, no words like refactor or regression. If a line only makes sense to someone who has read the source, it does not belong here. Newest first. Add an entry on every release that changes what people see.

releases.headline: Retake can now tell you whether your app actually looks right — and what keeps going wrong
notes: New: say what should be visible, and Retake checks it. On any scene you can write a plain sentence — "every card sits inside its own box", "the button's text is readable against its background" — and Retake puts that question to a second pair of eyes, against the actual frame it recorded. It answers yes or no, and tells you what it saw.

This is the check nothing else was doing. A page can pass every test, build clean, and still be broken in a way only a person notices: an animation frozen halfway, an icon that never loaded, a card that fell out of its grid, a label in dark text on a dark background. All four of those happened here in one day, and all four were caught by someone looking — not by anything the tools did. Now the tool looks.
The one judging it is never the one who made it. Retake asks a separate reader that sees only the picture and the question, so an agent cannot mark its own homework.

If it couldn't check, it says so rather than passing. No frame, nothing available to look at it, an answer it couldn't read — every one of those counts as a failure. A check that didn't run is not a check that passed.
Nothing changes unless you want it to. Demos without any of these sentences record exactly as before.

Also new: Retake reads your own recordings back to you. One command and it goes through every demo you have made and says the few things worth saying — a demo quietly showing live data when it was meant to show fake, the same button failing in five different demos because your app moved, a half-recording left sitting where the finished one should be, a demo nobody has ever checked the look of. It says nothing when there is nothing to say.
And when something it finds is really a habit rather than a one-off, it hands you a sentence to put in your agents' instructions — so the next agent does not repeat it.

releases.headline: You can see what your agent is doing, and it finishes what it started
notes: Captions are off by default now. A caption under the app makes you look away from the thing you came to watch, so a demo no longer paints them on unless you ask. Scene captions are still worth writing — they name the beats in the proof log and the stills.

Re-recording only what changed. Edit part of a demo you already recorded and Retake works out which scene your change starts at, then records from there instead of from the beginning. On a long demo that is a couple of minutes instead of eight.

Renders are much faster while you are still working on a demo. Skipping the archival copy took an eight-minute video from about eight minutes of encoding down to under three — and the video you hand over is very slightly better for it, because it is no longer a copy of a copy.

A progress bar while a demo records — how many steps in, how long it has been going, and roughly how long the render has left. The window used to just say "Recording…" and then nothing at all, sometimes for a quarter of an hour.
If your agent disconnects mid-recording, the recording now finishes and saves instead of dying halfway.
And if a recording is killed outright, it leaves a note saying which part it reached — so you can pick up from there instead of starting the whole thing again.
If a recording quietly stops making progress, the window says so — no step finished in 90 seconds — instead of leaving you guessing whether it is working or hung.
And if Retake gets updated while your agent is mid-session, it now tells the agent that it is running the older version and needs restarting, rather than silently missing the new behaviour.

releases.headline: Videos come out the size you asked for — and changing your mind is nearly free
notes: Every video is exactly the size of the format you picked. Landscape is 1920×1080, square is square, vertical fits a phone. No more sizes drifting between takes.
Changing your mind costs seconds, not another recording. Size, shape, format, captions, speed, zoom, music, title cards and the cover image all re-make themselves from the recording you already have.
Moved a caption to the wrong moment? Nudge it. The caption, the still and the cover all follow, and you never record again.

Only the ending changed? Record only the ending. The earlier steps still run so your app gets to the right place, but they happen at full speed and off camera. On a seven-minute demo that is about three minutes instead of sixteen.

Your old recordings are kept. A re-record no longer throws away the take you had — you can look at the previous ones and go back to any of them. Only the recording itself is stored, so it stays small.
A failed recording can no longer cost you the one that worked.
New: clear out old files safely. It shows you what it would free before removing anything, and never touches a recording.
In the window: pick several demos at once — or a whole folder — and archive them together. The archive empties in one click.
Launch videos can open with a title card and close with your own sign-off, put music underneath, and add a spoken voiceover.
Dead air gets trimmed: while your app is thinking, the video moves through the wait instead of sitting in it.
You can sign in to a demo account without any AI ever seeing your password.
Renders are about twice as fast.

Your agent now checks far more before recording — that a click will land on something clickable, that a stub is really being used, that it is looking at the same screen the recording will — so fewer takes are wasted finding out mid-recording.
On a long demo your agent shows you a quick draft and asks before spending the full recording.
The window has been rebuilt: one place for everything, and it stops shouting at you.

releases.headline: Demos behind a login
notes: Demos of apps that need signing in. You sign in once in a real browser window; nothing types your password and nothing records it.
The video player shows your video in its own shape, with no black bars around it.

releases.headline: The first public release
notes: Describe a demo in one readable file, and get a video, still frames, and a written record of what happened.
When your app changes, fix the file and run it again — instead of recording the whole thing over.
